q1: SELECT ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR GROUP BY ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID HAVING COUNT(*)>=3
q2: SELECT X.ACTOR_ID, X.DIRECTOR_ID FROM ( SELECT ACTOR_ID, DIRECTOR_ID, COUNT(*) FROM ACTORDIRECTOR GROUP BY ACTOR_ID, DIRECTOR_ID HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 ) X
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR GROUP BY ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID HAVING COUNT(*)>=3
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT X.ACTOR_ID, X.DIRECTOR_ID FROM ( SELECT ACTOR_ID, DIRECTOR_ID, COUNT(*) FROM ACTORDIRECTOR GROUP BY ACTOR_ID, DIRECTOR_ID HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 ) X
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are semantically equivalent. Both queries group the ACTORDIRECTOR table by ACTOR_ID and DIRECTOR_ID, filter groups where the count of rows in the group is >= 3, and return ACTOR_ID and DIRECTOR_ID. Q1 uses GROUP BY directly with HAVING, while Q2 uses a subquery that already performs the same GROUP BY and HAVING. The outer SELECT in Q2 has no effect since the subquery already produces the desired output. Therefore, both queries return the same result set.
